title: When Should Multi-Round RAG Stop? Structured Stopping Judgments and Retrieval Reduction in Search-R1
research_question: Can a structured sufficiency-and-gap judge change only the stopping time of a frozen multi-round Search-R1 trajectory to reduce retrieval while keeping answer-quality loss within a prespecified bound, and what stopping risk remains?
methodology: The study freezes Search-R1's reasoner, E5 top-3 retriever, Wiki-2018 corpus, prompt, and four-search budget, then constructs reachable retrieval states and labels whether a correct answer is already recoverable using a frozen answer-only probe. It trains a Qwen3.5-2B structured judge on 3,009 states from 900 disjoint HotpotQA training questions and selects its stopping threshold on grouped validation under a STOP-precision constraint. A held-out 800-question confirmatory evaluation applies the first threshold crossing on each trajectory and measures exact match, search calls, state-ranking quality, calibration, and safe versus unsafe early stops with paired bootstrap confidence intervals.

key_findings.finding: The confirmatory stopping policy removed 77 retrieval calls, reducing mean searches from 2.60125 to 2.50500, a 3.70% reduction, with the confidence interval satisfying the prespecified retrieval-reduction criterion.

Official exact match decreased from 0.44875 to 0.44250, a 0.625 percentage-point loss whose confidence interval remained inside the prespecified two-percentage-point noninferiority margin; this does not establish unchanged or improved accuracy.
Among 69 confirmatory early stops, 42 were classified as safe and 27 as unsafe, so 39.13% of the executed early stops were unsafe under the paper's probe-based definition.
The expanded structured judge improved STOP average precision over the structured-base judge, but validation STOP precision did not transfer to the final test set and calibration remained weak.

Exploratory trajectories contained substantial over-retrieval headroom: 143 of 523 native SEARCH actions occurred after the answer probe was already correct, and a native-preserving cost oracle could remove 131 searches while retaining native exact match.
Reducing retrieval calls is not equivalent to reducing total system cost because the additional judge introduces compute, memory, and latency that were not included in the retrieval-call metric.

limitations: The conclusions are conditional on a frozen Search-R1 configuration and a HotpotQA-based evaluation rather than a broad set of RAG systems and domains.
The learned stopping policy is not risk-certified: a substantial fraction of executed early stops were unsafe under the paper's own probe-based criterion.
The high validation STOP precision was based on a small number of positive stop predictions and did not transfer to the confirmatory set.
The evaluation counts retrieval calls but does not normalize end-to-end latency, token usage, memory, or judge-computation cost.

The correctness labels rely on a frozen answer-only probe, so they operationalize recoverability rather than proving that the retrieved evidence is complete or sufficient in a stronger semantic sense.

Per-question trajectories, benchmark-derived labels, and model weights are not redistributed in the reproduction repository, although the underlying benchmark and upstream resources remain available under their original licenses.
raw_claims: The paper treats multi-round RAG stopping as a sequential decision over already reachable reasoning and retrieval states.
A frozen answer-only probe is used to decide whether an official answer is already recoverable at a state.
The structured judge predicts sufficiency and evidence gaps without changing the underlying Search-R1 reasoner or retriever.
The judge was trained on 3,009 clean states derived from 900 HotpotQA training questions.
The confirmatory evaluation contains 800 held-out HotpotQA questions.
The learned policy reduced mean search calls by 0.09625 per question.
Official exact match fell by 0.00625 in absolute proportion.
Only a minority of available safe early-stop opportunities were actually captured by the learned policy.
Validation precision substantially overestimated confirmatory STOP precision.
The paper explicitly cautions that fewer searches do not by themselves demonstrate lower total inference cost.
